title: Autotune FP8 thresholds and validation path for Hopper E4M3/E5M2
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Scope: Build an automated autotuner and validation pipeline to pick E4M3 vs E5M2 FP8 profiles for Hopper GPUs across representative production workloads, plus a pragmatic stability guard and rollback path. This ticket owns the autotune algorithm, calibration data selection, quality validation harness, and operator-runbook for staged rollout.

Background: We have multiple manual calibration runs that indicate model/hyperparameter combinations prefer different FP8 profile selections. Manual selection is slow and brittle; we need automated thresholds and a repeatable accuracy validation path that matches runtime telemetry.

Goals and success criteria:
- Autotuner picks an FP8 profile (E4M3 or E5M2) per model-family and sequence-length bucket with 95% parity to FP32 accuracy on our eval suites (primary and edge prompts).
- End-to-end calibration and validation pipeline completes within target time (<= 4h for full model calibration on a 4-GPU testbed).
- Observability: per-profile accuracy deltas, token-level latency delta, and memory headroom surfaced to Console dashboards and used by rollout gating.
- Safety guard: a stability metric (see "stability_score") computed from variance across 5 independent calibration seeds; autotuner must fail safe if variance > threshold.

Approach:
1) Dataset & eval harness: select a compact representative prompt set (5k seed prompts) across ranking, generation, and instruction-following workloads. Store as s3://redwood-experiments/fp8/autotune/seedset-2025-01-07.jsonl and register in Confluence (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/FP8+Autotune+Seed+Sets).
2) Autotuner algorithm: grid search + heuristic early stopping. Start with both E4M3 and E5M2 profiles and run short calibration passes on a small shard (10%) to estimate variance; if stable, run full calibration. Heuristics encoded in autotune service (proto at github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8923).
3) Validation: run inference with quantized kernels and compare log-prob distributions and task-specific metrics against FP32 baseline. Primary validation metrics are BLEU/ROUGE for seq2seq, exact-match/EM for QA, and perplexity/language-modeling buckets for LM tasks. Dashboard query: Grafana panel linked from PR (https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/FP8/validation).
4) Operator runbook & rollout: progressive staged rollout: shadow -> litmus progressive -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on degradation > 1.5% absolute on primary metric or latency increase > 25%. Runbook draft in Confluence with explicit rollback commands and mitigations.

Acceptance criteria:
- PR merged that implements autotune service and CI job to run a nightly calibration (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4712).
- End-to-end test in dev cluster demonstrating selection for two model families (transformer-xl-1b and t5-3b) with documented results stored at s3 path above.
- Console dashboard shows profile assignment and stability_score for each model.

Risks & trade-offs:
- E5M2 yields lower memory but sometimes higher numeric instability for long sequences; tuning thresholds may bias toward E4M3 for tail workloads. We will expose a per-customer preference override in Dedicated/Private.
- Running full calibration across many models is expensive; we mitigate by incremental calibration and reusing cached prefix/KV statistics.

Next steps:
- Merge experimental PRs for autotuner service and validation harness (blocking: final review by runtime team).
- Run 3 production-like calibrations and collect variance metrics.
- Finalize runbook and rollout gating before runtime-1.20 release.
